thread.title: Apple Stock Spikes To Record High On News Of Sept. 12 iPhone Event

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Spikes To Record High On News Of Sept. 12 iPhone Event
text:
Apple stock surged to an all-time high Thursday after the consumer electronics giant announced a Sept. 12 event, presumably to reveal its latest iPhone models and other gadgets. Apple ( AAPL ) sent out its usual cryptic invitations to media and analysts midday for the fall product launch.
X Apple stock rose 0.9% to 225.03 on the stock market today. Earlier in the session, it hit a record high of 228.26.
The invitation features the message "Gather round" with a gold circle graphic that evokes the design of Apple's new corporate headquarters in Cupertino, Calif. The event will take place at 10 a.m. PT at the Steve Jobs Theater at the headquarters campus.
Analysts expect Apple to introduce three 12th-generation iPhones at the event. They include an updated version of the 5.8-inch OLED-screen iPhone X, a 6.5-inch OLED model and a 6.1-inch LCD-screen handset.

Please contact customer service CLOSE New iPhone Names Unknown Analysts are unsure what Apple will call the new handsets. They say this is probably an "S" year, in which the company makes incremental upgrades to its lineup. Starting with its third-generation model in 2009, Apple added an "S" to iPhones every other year.
But Apple deviated last year when it jumped to the iPhone 8 from the prior year's iPhone 7. It also added the flagship iPhone X, which celebrated the 10th anniversary of the first iPhone.
Apple also might launch its fourth-generation smartwatches at the annual event. The Apple Watch Series 4 is rumored to feature 15% larger displays and enhanced heart-rate detection.
Apple could use the event to introduce a new MacBook Air notebook computer and updated Mac Mini desktop computer and its latest iPad tablets, CNBC speculated .
Apple Buys AR Glasses Startup In other Apple news, Reuters reported that the company confirmed that it has purchased a startup focused on making lenses for augmented reality glasses. Apple bought Longmont, Colo.-based Akonia Holographics for an undisclosed sum.
Akonia's technology allows for "thin, transparent smart glass lenses that display vibrant, full-color, wide field-of-view images," its website says. The firm has a portfolio of more than 200 patents related to holographic systems and materials.
The acquisition indicates Apple wants to make AR glasses that can superimpose digital information on the real world.
